CAP-10.why: Multiple regimes (Quebec complaint regulation in force July 2025, Texas 13.492 seven-day deadlines, CIMA Corporate Governance/Internal Controls rules) impose fixed procedural deadlines and formats whose breach is a reportable compliance event, matching the strict-compliance band rather than general adherence.

CAP-11.why: Undetected errors in complaint handling, record retention, or vulnerable-customer monitoring under CIMA, Texas and FCA rules trigger regulatory attention or reportable breaches, not merely customer-level correction, matching the 'regulatory attention or reputational damage' band.

CAP-15.why: The Quebec complaint-handling regulation (effective July 1, 2025) newly mandates formal complaint policies and audit-ready records subject to regulator review, reaffirming rather than shifting the existing 'formal audit trail; regulator inspection' band.

CAP-11.why: Errors in complaint handling or record management in insurance trigger regulatory attention under regimes like the Quebec complaint regulation and CIMA's Internal Controls Rule, moving beyond internal rework to band 70 ('regulatory attention or reputational damage').

CAP-14.why: GDPR Article 9 classifies health data processed for insurance purposes as special-category data requiring specific safeguards (DPA 2018 Schedule 1 Para 20), matching band 70 ('special-category personal data, regulated financial or health records') rather than generic confidential data.

CAP-03.why: Insurance regulatory regimes (FCA Consumer Duty vulnerable-customer rules, multi-jurisdictional complaint/retention regimes) require the manager to recognise standard regulated cases (vulnerable customer status, complaint categorisation, retention triggers) rather than apply general knowledge, matching band 50 practitioner-level recognition rather than the generic band 30 familiarity.

evidence.regime: Insurance regulatory compliance including claims handling, complaints procedures, record retention, and vulnerable customer protections across multiple jurisdictions

sources.title: Regulation respecting complaint processing and dispute resolution in the financial sector
sources.rule: Entry into force July 1, 2025; requires firms to adopt a complaint handling policy and communicate it internally and externally, produce and distribute a summary to consumers, ensure fair handling of complaints, and send acknowledgment of receipt with specified information
sources.cite: Regulation respecting complaint processing and dispute resolution in the financial sector, Sections 5-10 and 30

sources.title: Rule on Corporate Governance for Regulated Entities and Rule and Statement of Guidance on Internal Controls for Regulated Entities
sources.rule: Section 5.7.5 of the Corporate Governance Rule and Sections 12.11 & 12.12 of the Internal Controls Rule and SOG prescribe requirements for complaints-handling framework that regulated entities must incorporate
sources.cite: Section 5.7.5 of the Corporate Governance Rule; Sections 12.11 & 12.12 of the Internal Controls Rule and SOG

sources.title: 28 Tex. Admin. Code § 13.492 - Complaints; Deadlines for Response and Resolution
sources.rule: An HCC must acknowledge receipt of a complaint in writing within seven calendar days, acknowledge the date of receipt, provide a description of complaint procedures and deadlines, and investigate each complaint in accord with its policies and Insurance Code § 848.107

sources.title: N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 11, Part 243 (Regulation 152)
sources.rule: A policy record for each insurance contract or policy must be retained for six calendar years after the policy is no longer in force or until the filing of the report on examination in which the record was subject to review, whichever is longer
sources.cite: N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 11, Part 243, Section 243.2(b)(1)

sources.title: N.Y. Ins. Law § 2119(a) & (c) and N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 11, § 20.4(b) & (c) (Regulation 29)
sources.rule: Record retention requirements for customer records of insurance agents and insurance brokers
sources.cite: N.Y. Ins. Law § 2119(a) & (c); N.Y. Comp. Codes R. & Regs. tit. 11, § 20.4(b) & (c)

sources.title: Proceeds of Crime Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) and associated Regulations
sources.rule: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents must meet record keeping obligations for purposes of PCMLTFA compliance with retention periods that cannot be shorter than specified requirements

sources.title: FCA Consumer Duty
sources.rule: Firms must monitor vulnerable customers over the product/service lifetime both reactively and proactively, maintain an evidence trail of changes, and notify the FCA where they become aware that another firm may not be complying with the Duty (PRIN 2A.2.22 R)
sources.cite: PRIN 2A.2.22 R and Consumer Duty requirements on vulnerable customer monitoring

sources.title: General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)
sources.rule: Article 9 prohibits processing of special category data including health data unless a legal basis applies; Article 9(2) provides exemptions including where processing is necessary for insurance purposes

sources.title: Data Protection Act 2018
sources.rule: Schedule 1 Para 20 authorizes processing of special category data where necessary for an insurance purpose; Part 4 of Schedule 1 requires data controllers to have in place an appropriate policy document and additional safeguards for handling special category data
